| `entity-resolution` **[C→`skills/entity-resolve`, `schema/validate.py`]** — thinnest skill in the catalog | `_brain-filing-rules.md` (notability, holder≠subject), harmonized with `entity-resolve/SKILL.md` | Holder≠subject epistemics (founder describing own company → holder is the founder); notability bar worded consistently with the existing internal skill |
| `entity-enrichment` | `enrich` (Hermes), `idea-ingest` (author-page rule) | Tiered effort scaling by importance; "texture over facts"; mandatory author-page creation |
| `note-routing` | `_brain-filing-rules.md`, `repo-architecture` | RESOLVER.md/SCHEMA.md split (entity routing = code, everything else = workspace file); no assumed phantom directories |
| `note-conformance` **[C→`schema/`, `wakil schema migrate`]** | `_output-rules.md`, `conventions/quality.md` (the two most authoritative, least self-contradictory per issue #7 — use only these two for citation format), `citation-fixer`, `note-taking/obsidian` (thin) | Three-part slug rule (defer to `slugify()`); one canonical link/citation format, verified against real code; no-slop output bar |
| `knowledge-query` | `query` (Hermes, primary), `brain-ops`/`conventions/brain-first.md`, `conventions/salience-and-recency.md` | Source precedence (user statement > compiled truth > timeline > external — matches `_stub_content()`'s real structure); recency-on-for-current-state vs off-for-canonical-truth |
| `knowledge-research` | `perplexity-research`, `academic-verify`, `research/arxiv` | "Dense, untruncated context or it's just a search"; 5-way verdict taxonomy for claim verification, folded in as an internal mode |
| `note-revision` | `conventions/quality.md` (primary — the "Scorealytics Regression" clobbering-bug lesson), `data-research` (dedup) | State=re-synthesize-as-union vs Timeline=append-only; 3-tier dedup; user-sovereignty (findings inform, never auto-apply) |
| `skill-authoring` | `skill-creator` + `skillify` (**reconciled into one standard, not both ported**), `functional-area-resolver`, `_AGENT_README.md`, `skillpack-harvest`, `retro` (ladder, rewritten) | MECE scan of the full filesystem before adding a skill; prefer extending over narrow new skills; override mechanism = `wakil skills list/which/validate`, not invented tooling |
| `kb-commit` | `knowledge-base/kb-commit` (kanban preamble, mem0 step, beads refs **stripped entirely**), `maintain` (confirm-before-destructive) | Real kind taxonomy (`wakil <kind>: <description>`); inspect-every-diff discipline; `wakil git summary`/`git history` as inspection commands |

## File layout

`src/wakil/skills/builtin/<name>/SKILL.md` for all 12 — clean create, `builtin/`
doesn't exist yet. Leave `src/wakil/skills/{article,text,transcript,entity-resolve}/`
untouched (different contract, different consumer).

Supporting subdirectories — resist adding these except where truly warranted
(extra structure without discipline is exactly the "competing standards, dangling
refs" pattern this migration exists to fix):

- `source-ingestion/references/` — per-source-type routing tables, keeps the body scannable
- `skill-authoring/templates/` — a blank SKILL.md scaffold
- All other 9 skills: single-file.

No skill needs `schemas/` or `scripts/` — schema enforcement is `src/wakil/schema/`,
not skill-local.

## Sanitization checklist — mandatory pass/fail gate, one item per cataloged issue

Every finished skill must pass all of:

1. No `gbrain` CLI/MCP references of any kind.
2. No hermes-kanban / `bd`/beads / task-tracking references.
3. No self-contradictory guidance (the specific failure mode: same example listed as
   both correct and incorrect).
4. No frontmatter template using `title:`/`type:` where wakil's schema requires
   `name:` (or vice versa) — verify any example frontmatter against
   `schema/validate.py`'s actual category rule.
5. No references to directories not backed by either the KB's real `RESOLVER.md` or
   `schema.directory` (no `originals/`, `personal/`, `deals/`, `media/x/`, etc.).
6. Exactly one skill-authoring standard, not two competing ones.
7. One canonical citation/link format, not several.
8. Every `related_skills`-style cross-reference names a skill that actually exists in
   the finished 12-skill catalog.
9. No directory-naming collisions (flat 12-skill layout should structurally prevent
   this, but confirm).

## Execution phasing

Dependency-ordered, not arbitrary batching — several skills must correctly *name*
sibling skills, so order matters for avoiding dangling references (checklist item 8).

- **Phase 0 — foundational reads, no output.** `conventions/quality.md`,
  `_output-rules.md`, the real `RESOLVER.md`, `entity-resolve/SKILL.md`,
  `article|text|transcript/SKILL.md`, `git_service.py`, `schema_migrate_service.py`,
  `ingest_service.py`. Every downstream skill must not contradict these.
- **Phase 1 — repository governance.** `note-routing`, `note-conformance` — referenced
  by nearly everything else; must be stable before anything names them.
- **Phase 2 — knowledge transformation**, foundational-first: `knowledge-query` before
  `knowledge-research` → `entity-resolution` before `entity-enrichment` → `note-revision`
  → `content-synthesis` → `source-ingestion` last within this phase (biggest fan-in,
  benefits from content-synthesis's boundary being settled).
- **Phase 3 — `ingest-source`**, last among transformation-layer skills — its pipeline
  diagram names the other six by name, so they must exist first.
- **Phase 4 — system operation.** `skill-authoring` and `kb-commit` in parallel, mostly
  independent of phases 1-3, but `skill-authoring` does a final pass after phase 3
  against the real finished set, and `kb-commit` benefits from `note-conformance` being
  final.
- **Phase 5 — mandatory cross-skill consistency pass.** One pass across all twelve,
  applying the sanitization checklist item-by-item as a pass/fail gate, plus checking
  terminology consistency (e.g. "entity page" vs. "entity note") and that every code
  reference (`wakil enrich`, `schema migrate`, `slugify()`, `COMMIT_PREFIXES`) is
  accurate against current source.

## Execution mechanism

A single Workflow, structured to match the phasing above — not a flat 12-way
fan-out. Flat fan-out risks each agent independently inventing slightly different
phrasing for shared concepts (notability gate, Iron Law of exact phrasing,
State-vs-Timeline, source precedence), recreating the citation-drift/competing-standards
problem *inside* the new catalog.

- Phase 0+1 as a short serial sequence (small count, referenced everywhere — get
  these right and stable first).
- Phase 2 as parallel per-skill authoring agents, each handed the finished Phase 0/1
  output plus a shared pinned "glossary" excerpt (exact wording of every cross-cutting
  principle) — not left to independent judgment.
- Phase 3 and Phase 4 as their own pass(es), each seeing the finished output of what
  they reference.
- Phase 5 as a dedicated review agent running the sanitization checklist item-by-item
  against the real wakil source tree (grep for banned patterns, verify every code
  reference), gating completion.
- Each authoring agent reads full source files for its assigned skill, not summaries
  — `conventions/quality.md` especially ("the corpus's core judgment") deserves a
  dedicated close read.
- One PR for all 12 files — they're interdependent, and reviewing "does skill X's
  cross-reference list match what actually exists" is much easier with the whole
  catalog in one diff.

## Verification

1. **`wakil skills validate`** — once `src/wakil/skills/builtin/` is populated, run
   this from a real (or scratch) workspace. All 12 should resolve with `source:
   builtin` and pass validation (frontmatter `name` matches directory, `skill_api:
   1`). This is a real, already-built verification tool — use it, don't just eyeball
   the files.
2. **`wakil skills list` / `wakil skills which <name> --verbose`** — spot-check a few
   names resolve to the expected path with no shadowing surprises.
3. **Sanitization checklist, mechanically** — grep the finished `builtin/` tree for
   `gbrain`, `bd `, `beads`, `mem0`, `hermes-kanban`, and the specific phantom
   directory names; all should return zero hits.
4. **Manual read-through against the content outline** — confirm each skill covers
   its outlined sections and correctly points at the code it's meant to defer to
   (spot-check a few file/function references actually exist as cited).
5. **Cross-reference check** — grep all 12 files for any skill-name-shaped reference,
   confirm each resolves to one of the 12 directories that actually exist.

export const meta = {
  name: 'skill-corpus-migration',
  description: 'Author wakil\'s 12-skill builtin catalog from the legacy Hermes skill corpus',
  phases: [

}

const REPO = '/Users/ebridges/Projects/wakil'
const HERMES = '/Users/ebridges/Projects/kb/.hermes/skills'
const KB_ROOT = '/Users/ebridges/Projects/kb'
const BUILTIN = `${REPO}/src/wakil/skills/builtin`

const CATALOG = [
  'ingest-source', 'source-ingestion', 'content-synthesis', 'entity-resolution',
  'entity-enrichment', 'note-routing', 'note-conformance', 'knowledge-query',
  'knowledge-research', 'note-revision', 'skill-authoring', 'kb-commit',

function commonRules(name) {
  return `
Repo: ${REPO} (wakil, a local-first Python CLI for a personal Markdown knowledge base).
You are authoring ONE file: ${BUILTIN}/${name}/SKILL.md — one entry in a 12-skill
"golden" catalog for wakil's skill-resolution system. Read
${REPO}/docs/skill-resolution-specification.md §4 and §8 for the exact contract if
useful, and read ${REPO}/.claude/skills/commit/SKILL.md first to calibrate tone.

AUDIENCE & VOICE: this file is read by an AI coding/knowledge agent (e.g. Claude
Code) working on a wakil-managed knowledge base. Write it as procedural instructions
FOR that agent to follow, in the same voice as .claude/skills/commit/SKILL.md above.
This is NOT end-user product documentation. Do not address "the user" as a reader —
address the agent that will follow these instructions.

FRONTMATTER CONTRACT — the file must start with:
---
name: ${name}
description: <one line: what this skill is for and when to use it>
skill_api: 1
---
\`name\` must be exactly "${name}". \`skill_api: 1\` is required. Do not add a
\`version\` field unless you have a real reason to.

SOURCE MATERIAL: for each directory/file named below (under ${HERMES} unless noted
otherwise), \`ls\` it first, then read its main definition file in FULL (usually
SKILL.md, sometimes a same-named .md or README.md; skim large examples/ or
templates/ subfolders only if load-bearing). This is a legacy corpus with real
hard-won judgment, but it's also rotted: it references a nonexistent "gbrain" CLI,
a task-tracking system wakil doesn't have, internally contradictory linking rules,
wrong frontmatter fields, and phantom directories. Extract the genuine judgment;
strip everything specific to the old system.

MANDATORY SANITIZATION CHECKLIST — your finished file must satisfy ALL of:
1. Zero references to "gbrain" (CLI or MCP tool names) anywhere.
2. Zero references to hermes-kanban, bd/beads, mem0, or any task-tracking system.
3. No self-contradictory guidance (e.g. the same example listed as both correct and
   incorrect — this is the exact bug in the source corpus's own RESOLVER.md).
4. Any example frontmatter you show must match wakil's real schema category rule:
   identity types use \`name:\` only, document types use \`title:\` only
   (src/wakil/schema/validate.py:62-69) — never invert this.
5. Never reference a directory (originals/, personal/, deals/, media/x/, etc.) unless
   it's backed by a real KB's RESOLVER.md or wakil's schema.directory values.
6. Only cross-reference (by name) skills that are actually in this 12-skill catalog:
   ${CATALOG.join(', ')}. Never invent a related-skill name, and never reference the
   internal DAG skills at src/wakil/skills/{article,text,transcript,entity-resolve}/
   as if they were part of this catalog (they're a separate mechanism).
7. Keep it THIN and high-signal, not an exhaustive manual. Prefer pointing at real
   wakil code/commands over restating what they already do deterministically.

When done, use the Write tool to create ${BUILTIN}/${name}/SKILL.md directly. Do not
run git commands. Do not create files for any other skill.
`
}

function glossaryBlock(glossary) {
  return `
SHARED GLOSSARY — use this EXACT wording (or a light paraphrase that preserves the
precise meaning) for these cross-cutting concepts wherever they appear in your file.
Other agents are authoring sibling skills from this same glossary; consistent wording
across the whole catalog matters more than your own phrasing preference here:

${glossary}
`
}

phase('Phase 0: Glossary')
const glossary = await agent(
  `Repo: ${REPO}. You are Phase 0 of a 12-skill catalog authoring effort (wakil's ` +
  `"golden" skills, replacing a legacy corpus at ${HERMES}). Your job: produce a ` +
  `short, precise GLOSSARY of cross-cutting concepts and verified code references ` +
  `that every other authoring agent will reuse verbatim, so the 12 finished skills ` +
  `don't each invent slightly different wording for the same ideas (that would ` +
  `recreate the citation-drift/competing-standards problem this whole migration ` +
  `exists to fix).\n\n` +
  `Read IN FULL: ${HERMES}/conventions/quality.md, ${HERMES}/_output-rules.md, ` +
  `${HERMES}/_brain-filing-rules.md, ${REPO}/src/wakil/skills/entity-resolve/SKILL.md, ` +
  `${REPO}/src/wakil/skills/article/SKILL.md, ${REPO}/src/wakil/app/git_service.py, ` +
  `${REPO}/src/wakil/schema/validate.py, ${REPO}/src/wakil/app/schema_migrate_service.py.\n` +
  `Skim: ${REPO}/src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py (the DAG + slugify()), ` +
  `${REPO}/src/wakil/app/search_service.py + query_service.py (the search/vsearch/query ` +
  `modes), ${REPO}/src/wakil/config/settings.py (SPECIAL_FILES), ${KB_ROOT}/RESOLVER.md ` +
  `lines 1-70 (to confirm the real self-contradiction: its "Correct" and "Incorrect" ` +
  `link-format lists both contain the identical wikilink example — the actual rule ` +
  `being botched is "no relative paths, always absolute from vault root," not a ` +
  `wikilink-vs-markdown-link conflict).\n\n` +
  `Produce EXACT wording (1-3 sentences each, ready to paste) for:\n` +
  `- The notability gate for creating a new entity page (harmonize with ` +
  `entity-resolve/SKILL.md's existing wording, don't drift from it)\n` +
  `- The holder≠subject epistemic rule (a founder describing their own company means ` +
  `the holder of the claim is the founder, not the company)\n` +
  `- The Iron Law of exact phrasing / back-linking discipline\n` +
  `- State (compiled truth, re-synthesize-as-union) vs Timeline (append-only) — ` +
  `include the "Scorealytics Regression" clobbering-bug lesson from quality.md as the ` +
  `cautionary example, in your own words\n` +
  `- Source precedence for answering questions: user statement > compiled truth > ` +
  `timeline > external\n` +
  `- The no-slop output bar (no filler/hedging/LLM preamble, exact-phrasing ` +
  `preservation, title-quality rules) — cite the two most authoritative source docs ` +
  `only (quality.md + _output-rules.md), not the corpus's other conflicting citation ` +
  `guidance\n` +
  `- The extraction-integrity rule (never trust LLM working memory for figures/` +
  `amounts, always re-read saved raw files)\n` +
  `- Test-3-5-before-bulk discipline\n` +
  `- The canonical link format: confirm from storage/schema.py or prompts.py how ` +
  `wakil actually models links, and state ONE rule (absolute-from-vault-root, per the ` +
  `real non-contradictory reading above)\n\n` +
  `Also produce a VERIFIED CODE REFERENCES list (exact file paths / function or ` +
  `constant names, confirmed by reading, not guessed) for: the commit-kind taxonomy ` +

  { phase: 'Phase 0: Glossary', label: 'glossary' }

const GLOSSARY = glossaryBlock(glossary)

phase('Phase 1: Governance')
const [noteRouting, noteConformance] = await parallel([
  () => agent(
    commonRules('note-routing') + GLOSSARY +

    `${HERMES}/repo-architecture/ (ls it, read the main file). Also read ` +
    `${KB_ROOT}/RESOLVER.md's "Concept vs Project" section (around lines 1-45) as a ` +

    `CONTENT OUTLINE:\n` +
    `- What this skill decides: where a note belongs. It does NOT define page ` +
    `structure (that's note-conformance's job) — state this boundary explicitly, ` +
    `matching docs/skill-refactor.md's own wording for the distinction.\n` +
    `- The RESOLVER.md/SCHEMA.md split: entity-type routing is code-owned ` +

    `everything else (raw sources, synthesized notes, journal entries, meeting ` +
    `records), the KB's own RESOLVER.md (if present, one of wakil's SPECIAL_FILES) is ` +
    `the sole authority; if absent, ask the user rather than assuming a destination.\n` +
    `- Primary-subject-not-format filing principle, with the sui-generis-synthesis ` +

    `- The notability gate (from the glossary) as it applies to routing decisions.\n` +
    `- A short decision-tree template for "where does this new file go," generalized ` +

    `real RESOLVER.md or schema.directory would supply.\n` +
    `- Explicit statement: never assume a destination directory that isn't backed by ` +
    `the KB's actual RESOLVER.md or a schema.directory value.`,
    { phase: 'Phase 1: Governance', label: 'note-routing' }
  ),
  () => agent(
    commonRules('note-conformance') + GLOSSARY +
    `\n\nSOURCES for note-conformance: ${HERMES}/_output-rules.md, ` +
    `${HERMES}/conventions/quality.md, ${HERMES}/citation-fixer/ (ls, read main file), ` +
    `${HERMES}/note-taking/obsidian/ (ls, read main file — thin section only, mostly ` +
    `tool-usage mechanics). Also read ${REPO}/src/wakil/schema/validate.py and ` +
    `${REPO}/src/wakil/app/schema_migrate_service.py in full, plus skim the ` +
    `\`schema migrate\` CLI command in ${REPO}/src/wakil/cli/main.py.\n\n` +
    `CONTENT OUTLINE — keep this skill DELIBERATELY THIN, it defers to real code for ` +
    `most of its mandate:\n` +
    `- When to run \`wakil schema migrate --dry-run\` vs. hand-edit a note; what it ` +

    `stay prose judgment, covered below).\n` +
    `- The identity/document/hybrid category split — point at ` +
    `src/wakil/schema/validate.py's actual rule (name: vs title:), don't restate a ` +
    `hand-written frontmatter rule.\n` +
    `- The canonical link/citation format from the glossary — state it once, clearly, ` +
    `as the only accepted format.\n` +
    `- Three-part slug rule (filename/H1/wikilink must all match, lowercase-kebab), ` +
    `pointing at slugify() as the implementation.\n` +
    `- The no-slop output bar from the glossary (no filler, exact-phrasing ` +
    `preservation, title quality).\n` +
    `- Deterministic links only — never guess a URL; flag rather than delete an ` +
    `uncitable fact.`,
    { phase: 'Phase 1: Governance', label: 'note-conformance' }
  ),
])
log('note-routing and note-conformance written; starting knowledge-transformation skills.')

phase('Phase 2: Transformation')

const [knowledgeQuery, entityResolution] = await parallel([
  () => agent(
    commonRules('knowledge-query') + GLOSSARY +
    `\n\nSOURCES for knowledge-query: ${HERMES}/query/ (ls, read main file), ` +
    `${HERMES}/brain-ops/ (ls, read main file — extract ONLY the brain-first lookup ` +
    `chain section, the rest of brain-ops is out of scope / belongs to other skills), ` +
    `${HERMES}/conventions/brain-first.md, ${HERMES}/conventions/salience-and-recency.md. ` +

    `skim ${REPO}/src/wakil/cli/main.py's \`search\`/\`query\` commands.\n\n` +
    `CONTENT OUTLINE:\n` +
    `- QMD/FTS as an implementation detail behind \`wakil search\` / \`wakil query\` — ` +
    `this skill's job is deciding WHICH mode to use and how to read results, not how ` +

    `- The three real modes and when to reach for each (search=BM25 default, ` +
    `vsearch=semantic/vector, query=hybrid) — author this section FRESH against the ` +
    `real modes; do NOT port the source corpus's three named cost bundles ` +

    `- Source precedence (from the glossary): user statement > compiled truth > ` +
    `timeline > external.\n` +
    `- Recency/salience axis: on for current-state questions, off for canonical-truth ` +
    `questions; an explicit temporal bound in the question always overrides the default.\n` +
    `- Distinguish retrieved fact from inference; disclose incomplete/conflicting ` +

    `- Brain-first lookup order: search the KB before reaching for any external tool.`,
    { phase: 'Phase 2: Transformation', label: 'knowledge-query' }
  ),
  () => agent(
    commonRules('entity-resolution') + GLOSSARY +
    `\n\nSOURCES for entity-resolution: ${HERMES}/_brain-filing-rules.md (notability + ` +
    `holder≠subject sections). Also read ${REPO}/src/wakil/skills/entity-resolve/SKILL.md ` +

## 1. Notability gate (entity creation)

> Before creating a new entity page, check notability: will you interact

## 2. Holder ≠ subject (epistemic attribution rule)

> The holder of a claim is whoever said or clearly implied it, not whoever
> the claim is about. When a founder describes their own company, the

## 4. State vs. Timeline, and the Scorealytics Regression

> A knowledge page has two regions with opposite update disciplines. State
> (Compiled Truth) is *re-synthesized* on every update to cover the union of
> what was already there plus new facts — rewriting the State section means
> re-deriving it from everything known, never replacing it with only the

1	---
2	name: entity-resolution
3	description: Match a person, company, project, or concept a source or note refers to against existing knowledge-base entities — confident match, no match, or ambiguous. Use before adding a link, a stub page, or a frontmatter reference to any entity.
4	skill_api: 1
5	---
6	
7	# entity-resolution
8	
9	This skill answers one narrow question: **does this referenced entity
10	correspond to an existing knowledge-base page, and if not, does it warrant
11	one?** It does not decide which links a note should carry, how many, or
12	where they go — that judgment belongs to `entity-enrichment`. Keep the two
13	separate:
14	
15	```text
16	entity-resolution → determine what an entity refers to
17	entity-enrichment → decide how the note should connect to it
18	```
19	
20	If you're asking "what page is this?", you're in this skill. If you're
21	asking "should this note link to it, and how?", you're past this skill's
22	scope — hand the resolution result to `entity-enrichment`.
23	
24	## When to use
25	
26	- Any time a note, source, or edit mentions a person, company, project, or
27	  concept and you need to know whether it already has a page before
28	  proposing a link, a stub, or a frontmatter `ref` field.
29	- Most directly during `note-revision` and manual editing — anywhere an
30	  agent is touching a note by hand, outside `wakil enrich`.
31	
32	## The CLI path already does this — don't duplicate it
33	
34	`wakil enrich <source-id>` runs entity resolution as a fixed DAG step,
35	always invoked, never optional (`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`,
36	`_run_entity_resolution`). It calls the internal
37	`skills/entity-resolve/SKILL.md` judgment against every entity the
38	extraction step surfaced, then `_build_stub_entities` turns each
39	`action: create` result into a schema-routed stub page, and
40	`validate_proposal()` hard-stops on any entity type the schema doesn't
41	recognize rather than best-guessing a shape. If you're driving ingestion
42	through `wakil ingest` / `wakil enrich`, that mechanism already applies this
43	judgment — don't re-run it by hand.
44	
45	This skill exists for everywhere else: `note-revision`, ad hoc editing, or
46	any other case where an agent is resolving an entity mention outside that
47	pipeline. The judgment below is the same one `entity-resolve` encodes for
48	the CLI path — apply it consistently so a note edited by hand and a note
49	produced by `wakil enrich` don't disagree about whether "Jane" is
50	`people/jane-doe.md`.
51	
52	## Decision procedure
53	
54	For each entity a source or note touches, resolve independently — one
55	transcript or note routinely touches several entities (a person, their
56	company, a project) at once; don't collapse them into one destination.
57	Reach exactly one of three outcomes:
58	
59	- **Confident match.** An existing page corresponds to this entity. Match
60	  by identity, not string equality: "Jane," "Jane Doe," and a stored
61	  `people/jane-doe.md` with `aliases: [Jane]` are the same person if
62	  context supports it. Point at the page's exact path; do not restate or
63	  guess at its frontmatter.
64	- **No match, and it clears the notability gate.** No page exists yet, but
65	  the entity is worth one — see below. Surface this as a create candidate
66	  for `entity-enrichment` to act on; don't create the page yourself as a
67	  side effect of resolving identity.
68	- **No match, and it doesn't clear the gate, or it's genuinely
69	  ambiguous.** A drive-by mention, or a name that fits two existing pages
70	  (or two entity types) with nothing in the source to settle it. Surface
71	  it as unresolved rather than guessing.
72	
73	## Notability gate
74	
75	Before treating an unmatched entity as a create candidate, apply the same
76	bar `entity-resolve` uses: will you interact with this person again, or are
77	they relevant to your work or interests? Is the company relevant to work,
78	job search, or interests? Is the concept a reusable mental model worth
79	referencing again? A page clears the gate when it's likely to accumulate
80	history — a colleague the user will meet again, a company under evaluation,
81	a concept the source substantially develops. It doesn't clear the gate when
82	it's a drive-by mention — a name appearing once with no role in what
83	happened, a company named only as someone's past employer, a concept
84	mentioned but not developed.
85	
86	When in doubt, don't propose creation. A missing page can be created later
87	once the entity actually recurs; a junk page sits in every future search
88	result and degrades retrieval for everything else.
89	
90	## Holder ≠ subject
91	
92	When the source or note attributes a claim to someone, the entity you're
93	resolving as the claim's holder is whoever said or clearly implied it, not
94	whoever the claim is about. A founder describing their own company's
95	prospects is the holder — companies don't speak, their employees do. If
96	you're resolving "who is this claim attributed to" as part of matching, do
97	not resolve it to the company just because the company is the claim's
98	subject; resolve it to the person who made the statement, and let the
99	company be a separate entity if it's independently referenced.
100	
101	## Never auto-merge
102	
103	Do not resolve an ambiguous case by picking whichever candidate matched
104	first, and do not merge two existing pages into one because they look
105	similar. An entity that genuinely fits two existing pages, or fits none
106	cleanly, is more useful surfaced as ambiguous than silently collapsed into
107	a wrong match — a bad merge is harder to undo than an unresolved mention,
108	because it corrupts both pages' history. Preserve the ambiguity and let
109	`entity-enrichment` or the calling agent decide how to handle it (skip the
110	link, ask, or leave a flagged note).
111

1	---
2	name: kb-commit
3	description: Commit pending changes in a wakil-managed knowledge base with wakil's kind-prefixed message convention, grouped into reviewable logical change sets. Use after manual edits, after note-revision, or after a schema migrate run that wasn't committed inline.
4	skill_api: 1
5	---
6	
7	# kb-commit
8	
9	This skill governs commits to a **knowledge-base workspace** wakil manages — not
10	commits to wakil's own source code. It is a different convention from whatever
11	governs this dev repo's own history; do not blend the two.
12	
13	`wakil ingest`, `wakil enrich`, and `wakil schema migrate` each have their own
14	`--branch`/`--commit` flags and already commit their own output correctly when
15	those flags are passed. This skill exists for what those flags don't cover:
16	manual edits to a note, output from a `note-revision` pass, or a
17	`schema migrate` run made without `--commit`. If a wakil command's own commit
18	flag is available and appropriate for the change at hand, prefer it over this
19	skill — this is the fallback path, not the default one.
20	
21	## When to use
22	
23	- After hand-editing one or more notes directly (not through `wakil ingest`).
24	- After a `content-synthesis` or `note-revision` pass leaves the working tree
25	  dirty.
26	- After `wakil schema migrate` was run without `--commit`.
27	- Any other point where the knowledge-base working tree has changes wakil
28	  itself didn't already commit.
29	
30	## The commit convention
31	
32	Every commit message is `wakil <kind>: <description>`, produced by
33	`commit_message()` in `src/wakil/app/git_service.py`. `kind` must be one of
34	`COMMIT_PREFIXES`:
35	
36	```python
37	COMMIT_PREFIXES = ("ingest", "note", "link", "memory", "dream", "source", "chore")
38	```
39	
40	An unrecognized kind is a hard error there (`GitServiceError: unknown commit
41	kind: ...`), not a warning — treat the list above as closed, don't invent a new
42	kind for a commit this skill produces.
43	
44	What each kind is for, going by how wakil's own code already uses them:
45	
46	- **`source`** — a raw capture added under `sources/`, before enrichment.
47	  `commit_ingest`'s docstring: *"'source' for raw captures, 'ingest' for
48	  enrichment output."*
49	- **`ingest`** — enrichment output: the note(s)/entities a `wakil enrich` run
50	  produced from a source. Under this skill, use it for a manually-applied
51	  enrichment result you're committing by hand.
52	- **`note`** — a manual edit to an existing note, or a `note-revision` result:
53	  a compiled-truth (State) rewrite, a Timeline append, a prose fix. This is
54	  the kind you'll reach for most often under this skill.
55	- **`link`** — adding or repairing cross-references/back-links without
56	  otherwise changing a note's content.
57	- **`chore`** — tooling, config, schema fixes. This is the kind
58	  `schema_migrate_service.py` itself uses (see `note-conformance`'s
59	  "Mechanical fixes" section) — reuse it for the same class of change when
60	  committing a migrate run by hand.
61	- **`memory`** — a memory-lifecycle change (candidate → active promotion,
62	  a memory record's retirement) as described in `docs/memory-model.md`.
63	- **`dream`** — output of a periodic re-synthesis/consolidation pass, once
64	  that command exists (see `TODO.md`'s `wakil dream` entries). Not yet
65	  produced by any shipped wakil command as of this writing; use `note` or
66	  `ingest` for anything currently generated.
67	
68	There is no general-purpose `wakil commit` CLI command — `commit_message()` is
69	a library function invoked by `ingest`/`enrich`/`schema migrate`'s own
70	`--commit` flag and by this skill's manual `git commit` calls alike. Match its
71	output exactly (`wakil <kind>: <description>`) rather than inventing a
72	different shape for a hand-run commit.
73	
74	## Procedure
75	
76	1. **Survey.** Run `wakil git summary` for branch, pending-change count, and
77	   recent commit context. For any single file whose history you need to
78	   understand before deciding where it belongs, `wakil git history <path>`
79	   shows its prior commits.
80	
81	2. **Inspect every diff individually before grouping.** `git status
82	   --porcelain` gives the file list; `git diff --stat` gives shape — neither
83	   is enough to decide grouping. Open the actual diff (`git diff <path>`, or
84	   read the first ~30 lines of an untracked file) for every changed path
85	   before deciding which change set it belongs to. Do not `git add -A` and
86	   commit as one blob — a note edit and an unrelated frontmatter fix picked
87	   up in the same sweep is exactly the failure mode this step prevents.
88	
89	3. **Group into logical change sets.** One coherent concern per commit:
90	   a single note's revision, one batch of related back-link additions, one
91	   schema-migrate type's mechanical fixes. Different notes touched for
92	   unrelated reasons are different commits even if they landed in the same
93	   session.
94	
95	4. **Exclude transient, generated, or sensitive files.** Don't stage SQLite
96	   WAL/journal files, caches, or anything that looks like local credentials —
97	   if something like that shows up modified, it's a sign it doesn't belong in
98	   this repo at all, not something to sweep into a commit. When in doubt,
99	   surface it and ask rather than silently staging or silently dropping it.
100	
101	5. **Confirm before committing.** State the proposed change sets (message +
102	   files) and get explicit approval before running `git commit` — this
103	   applies even to a single obviously-correct commit. Never commit
104	   destructive changes (a deletion, a large rewrite) without the user having
105	   seen the diff first. This mirrors wakil's own preview/confirm/apply
106	   discipline (`schema_migrate_service.py`'s propose → diff → confirm →
107	   apply split) — don't hold this skill to a lower bar than the code it's
108	   filling a gap around.
109	
110	6. **Write the message to describe the knowledge change, not the file list.**
111	   The subject line is `wakil <kind>: <description>` in imperative,
112	   lowercase-first, no trailing period. The description names what changed
113	   about the knowledge base ("resynthesize Acme Corp state after Q3
114	   update-call transcript", not "update acme-corp.md"). Add a body when the
115	   change isn't self-explanatory from the subject alone — what triggered it,
116	   what source it came from, what was added versus revised.
117	
118	7. **Commit each group, then re-verify.** After each commit, `git status
119	   --porcelain` again before staging the next group — confirm only the
120	   intended files moved and nothing unexpected is still sitting dirty.
121	
122	8. **Do not push** unless explicitly asked.
123	
124	## Examples
125	
126	```
127	wakil note: resynthesize Acme Corp state from Q3 update call
128	
129	State section re-derived from the existing page plus the 2026-07-14
130	transcript; prior distilled history and Timeline entries preserved,
131	not replaced.
132	```
133	
134	```
135	wakil link: back-link Jane Doe from the Acme Corp Q3 meeting note
136	```
137	
138	```
139	wakil chore: apply schema migrate field renames for organization/ notes
140	
141	end_date -> end-date, start_date -> start-date across 6 files, per
142	`wakil schema migrate --dry-run --type organization`.
143	```
144	
145	```
146	wakil source: add raw transcript for 2026-07-14 Acme Corp update call
147	```
148	
149	## Related skills
150	
151	- `note-revision` and `content-synthesis` produce the edits this skill
152	  commits; run this skill after their output, not instead of them.
153	- `note-conformance` should already have passed on a note before it's
154	  committed here — a schema-invalid or badly-slugged note is a conformance
155	  problem, not a commit-message problem.
156

1	---
2	name: note-conformance
3	description: Audit a note's frontmatter, slug, links, and prose against wakil's schema and output-quality bar, and fix what's mechanical or flag what isn't. Use after drafting or revising a note, or when auditing existing pages for schema/prose drift.
4	skill_api: 1
5	---
6	
7	# note-conformance
8	
9	This is a checking skill, not a content-generating one. `content-synthesis` and
10	`note-revision` decide what a note says; `note-conformance` is the pass that
11	verifies the result is shaped correctly before it goes through `kb-commit` —
12	schema-valid frontmatter, a consistent slug, deterministic links, and prose
13	that meets the no-slop bar. Run it on one note at a time; it produces a short
14	list of fixes applied and issues flagged, not a rewrite.
15	
16	## When to use
17	
18	- After drafting a new note or substantially revising an existing one.
19	- Before `kb-commit`, as a last check on anything about to be written to the
20	  knowledge base.
21	- When explicitly asked to audit existing pages for drift (stale frontmatter
22	  casing, mismatched slugs, missing citations).
23	
24	For frontmatter drift across many notes at once, prefer `wakil schema migrate`
25	(below) over hand-editing every file — let the deterministic tool do the
26	mechanical part, and reserve this skill's judgment for what it can't cover.
27	
28	## Procedure
29	
30	1. **Run the mechanical pass first.** For the note's entity type, run
31	   `wakil schema migrate --dry-run --type <type>` and read the diff. Apply it
32	   (`--yes` or per-file confirm) before doing anything by hand — see
33	   "Mechanical fixes" below for exactly what this does and doesn't cover.
34	2. **Check the category rule.** Confirm `name:` vs `title:` matches the
35	   entity's schema category — see "Category rule" below. This is a hard
36	   schema error, not a style preference.
37	3. **Check the three-part slug.** Filename, H1, and every wikilink pointing
38	   at this note must agree — see "Slug consistency" below.
39	4. **Check links.** Internal cross-references are `[[path]]` wikilinks using
40	   the note's full workspace-relative path; external links are copied
41	   verbatim from their source, never reconstructed. See "Links" below.
42	5. **Check prose against the no-slop bar.** No filler, no hedged citations,
43	   no LLM preamble, no placeholder dates, exact phrasing preserved where the
44	   phrasing is the insight, titles under 60 characters and specific. See
45	   "No-slop output bar" below.
46	6. **Report, don't silently resolve, what you can't fix.** A fact with no
47	   traceable source, an entity type unknown to the schema, an ambiguous
48	   frontmatter conflict — flag these explicitly rather than guessing or
49	   deleting. See "Deterministic links, uncitable facts" below.
50	
51	## Mechanical fixes: `wakil schema migrate`
52	
53	`wakil schema migrate` (`src/wakil/app/schema_migrate_service.py`) is the
54	cheap tier only: mechanical fixes a linter could make, not judgment calls.
55	Concretely, per file, it:
56	
57	- renames casing/naming duplicates (`end_date`→`end-date`, `start_date`→
58	  `start-date`, `linkedin-link`→`linkedin`, `authors`→`author`, `link`→`url`),
59	  dropping the old key only when it's an exact duplicate value — a genuine
60	  conflict (both present, different values) is left in place and surfaced,
61	  never silently resolved;
62	- retypes `organization/`-directory files that were declared `type: concept`
63	  back to `type: organization`;
64	- aligns a mechanically re-cased `title` back to an authored-case `name` when
65	  they differ only by casing (guards a title-caser artifact like `1NSP` →
66	  `1nsp` without touching a genuinely different title);
67	- normalizes a quoted `type: "..."` value.
68	
69	It does **not** touch page structure, section shape, exact-phrasing
70	preservation, or title quality — those stay this skill's prose judgment (see
71	"No-slop output bar"). It also never retypes an unknown `type` or resolves an
72	ambiguous rename; those are always left for manual review.
73	
74	Run it with `--dry-run` first and read the diff before applying — this is
75	`wakil`'s own implementation of test-the-sample-before-the-batch discipline:
76	`plan_schema_migration` only proposes (nothing is touched during planning),
77	and `apply_migrations` re-reads each file immediately before writing,
78	skipping any file that changed on disk since the plan was made rather than
79	overwriting it blind. Use `--type <type>` to scope a run to one entity type,
80	`--yes` to apply without per-file confirmation once you've reviewed the plan,
81	and `--commit` to have each type's fixes land as its own `wakil chore: ...`
82	commit.
83	
84	## Category rule: `name:` vs `title:`
85	
86	The identity/document split is enforced in code
87	(`src/wakil/schema/validate.py:62-69`), not by convention — get it wrong and
88	`validate_frontmatter` returns a hard `SchemaError`, not a warning:
89	
90	- **identity** types (e.g. `person`, `company`) use `name:` only. A `title:`
91	  field on an identity type is an error.
92	- **document** types (e.g. `meeting`) use `title:` only. A `name:` field on a
93	  document type is an error.
94	
95	```yaml
96	# identity type (src/wakil/schema/entities/person.yaml) — name only
97	---
98	type: person
99	name: Jane Doe
100	status: active
101	created: 2026-07-16
102	updated: 2026-07-16
103	---
104	```
105	
106	```yaml
107	# document type (src/wakil/schema/entities/meeting.yaml) — title only
108	---
109	type: meeting
110	title: Q3 planning sync
111	date: 2026-07-16
112	created: 2026-07-16
113	---
114	```
115	
116	An `entity_type` the schema doesn't recognize is itself a hard error — don't
117	best-guess a schema for an unfamiliar `type:`; flag it.
118	
119	## Slug consistency
120	
121	A note's slug appears in three places, and all three must be the same
122	lowercase-kebab string:
123	
124	1. the filename (minus `.md`);
125	2. the H1 heading at the top of the note body;
126	3. every `[[wikilink]]` elsewhere in the knowledge base that points at this
127	   note.
128	
129	`slugify()` (`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py:661`) is the reference
130	implementation wakil itself uses (and `git_service.py` reuses for branch
131	names): lowercase, non-alphanumeric runs collapsed to a single `-`, leading
132	and trailing `-` stripped. Use it as the definition of "correctly slugged,"
133	not a separate hand-rolled rule. A note whose H1 is Title Case, or whose
134	filename and H1 disagree, is a conformance failure — fix the drifting one to
135	match the filename, don't rename the file to match a stray heading.
136	
137	## Links
138	
139	**Internal cross-references** use the wikilink form `[[path]]`, where `path`
140	is the note's full workspace-relative path — never a bare filename, never a
141	title string, and never a path built relative to the linking file (no
142	`../...`). `schema/validate.py`'s `ref` field kind only checks that a
143	reference is a string; resolving it to an actual note is the knowledge
144	base's own `RESOLVER.md` (a workspace-provided file wakil reads, not one it
145	ships) — defer to whatever path/slug convention the open workspace's
146	`RESOLVER.md` states, but the "absolute path from the vault root, never
147	relative" rule itself is non-negotiable regardless of workspace.
148	
149	**External links** are copied verbatim from their source — see "Deterministic
150	links" below.
151	
152	## No-slop output bar
153	
154	Notes are durable artifacts, not chat output:
155	
156	- No filler phrases ("It's worth noting that...", "Interestingly...").
157	- No hedging when a fact is cited — "X is true" per the source, not "X might
158	  be true."
159	- No LLM preamble ("I've created...", "Here's the updated...", "Certainly!").
160	- No placeholder dates ("recently," an unfilled `YYYY-MM-DD`).
161	- Preserve a speaker's exact words rather than paraphrasing when their
162	  phrasing is itself the insight — don't clean up grammar or swap in your
163	  own terminology for a person's own framework or coinage.
164	- Titles are descriptive enough to find in a search result, under 60
165	  characters, not full sentences, and not generic ("Jane Doe, VP Eng at
166	  Acme" not "Person Page").
167	
168	## Deterministic links, uncitable facts
169	
170	Never guess or reconstruct a URL — a wikilink is built from the note's actual
171	path, an external link is copied from the source that supplied it, never
172	composed from a slug or a memory of what the URL "should" be.
173	
174	When a fact has no traceable source, or a link can't be built deterministically,
175	**flag it rather than inventing a citation or silently deleting the fact.**
176	Both failure modes are worse than an honest gap: a fabricated source misleads
177	every future reader, and a deleted fact is knowledge the base quietly loses.
178

gh pr create --title "Add the 12-skill builtin catalog (skill-refactor.md)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Populates `src/wakil/skills/builtin/` — the skill resolver's lowest-precedence
root, previously empty — with the 12-skill "golden" catalog defined in
`docs/skill-refactor.md`: `ingest-source`, `source-ingestion`,
`content-synthesis`, `entity-resolution`, `entity-enrichment`, `note-routing`,
`note-conformance`, `knowledge-query`, `knowledge-research`, `note-revision`,
`skill-authoring`, `kb-commit`.

Each skill migrates working judgment out of a legacy corpus
(`~/Projects/kb/.hermes/skills`, ~59 files, used by an older agent
orchestrator) that `skill-refactor.md` documents as rotted: fictional
`gbrain` CLI calls scattered across ~20+ files, a 3-way task-tracking
split-brain, an internally self-contradictory `RESOLVER.md`, schema
violations baked into templates, phantom directories, two competing
un-cross-referenced skill-authoring standards, and citation-format drift.
None of that ported — every file was authored fresh from the source
material's genuine judgment, grounded against wakil's actual code.

Where wakil already implements something deterministically (entity schema
validation, the ingest/enrich DAG, `wakil schema migrate`, the real
commit-kind taxonomy, the search/vsearch/query modes), the corresponding
skill is a thin pointer into that code rather than re-derived judgment —
e.g. `entity-resolution` is ~110 lines and mostly says "the CLI already
does this, here's how it applies outside that path," while `kb-commit`
documents wakil's real `wakil <kind>: <description>` convention
(`git_service.COMMIT_PREFIXES`) instead of the source corpus's emoji
taxonomy.

Full planning rationale, source-to-target mapping, and the grounding
research live in the approved plan for this work (session transcript);
happy to write that up as a doc if useful.

## Process

Built via a 6-phase Workflow mirroring the skill catalog's real dependency
graph (not a flat fan-out): a foundational glossary pass pins exact wording
for cross-cutting concepts (notability gate, holder≠subject, State-vs-
Timeline, source precedence, etc.) that every subsequent agent reuses
verbatim, so the 12 files don't independently drift on the same ideas the
way the legacy corpus did. Governance skills (`note-routing`,
`note-conformance`) went first since almost everything else references
them; `ingest-source` went last among the content skills since its pipeline
diagram names the other six by name. A final mandatory consistency-gate
agent re-read all 12 files against a 10-item sanitization checklist derived
directly from `skill-refactor.md`'s "Existing skill issues" section, fixing
any violation found, before running the real `wakil skills` CLI as a
pass/fail check.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run wakil skills list` / `skills validate` against a scratch
      workspace — all 12 resolve with `source: builtin` and validate clean
      (exit 0) — ran independently, not just trusting the workflow's own
      report
- [x] `uv build` — confirmed all 14 files (12 `SKILL.md` + 2 supporting
      files) are actually included in the built wheel, not just present in
      this editable checkout
- [x] Sanitization greps (`gbrain`, `hermes-kanban`/`bd`/`beads`/`mem0`,
      phantom directories `originals/`/`personal/`/`deals/`/`media/x/`) —
      all clean
- [x] Cross-reference matrix — every skill-name reference across all 12
      files resolves to a real catalog member; the only non-catalog name
      (`entity-resolve`, wakil's separate internal DAG-judgment skill) is
      correctly documented as an internal mechanism, not a catalog member
- [x] Frontmatter check — all 12 have `name` matching their directory and
      `skill_api: 1`
- [x] Spot-read `entity-resolution`, `kb-commit`, and `note-conformance` in
      full against the source code they cite (`COMMIT_PREFIXES`,
      `schema/validate.py`'s category rule, `slugify()`, `entity-resolve`'s
      notability wording) — all accurate, no hallucinated APIs

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)"
